# Citation

Zappia, L., Phipson, B., and Oshlack, A. (2017). *Splatter: simulation of single-cell RNA sequencing data*. Genome Biology. DOI: 10.1186/s13059-017-1305-0. Source: [https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5596896/](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5596896/).

# One-Sentence Summary

Introduces Splatter, a framework for simulating single-cell RNA-seq count data with biological and technical variability.

# Scope for simitall

Use as a reference and possible backend for generic single-cell count simulations. simitall should add genotype, family, condition, and eQTL truth before handing off to a technical simulator.

# Agent-Safe Takeaways

- Single-cell simulation should expose library size, dispersion, dropout, and group effects.
- A count matrix needs cell-level metadata and known cell-type labels for evaluation.
- Generic scRNA-seq variation is not the same as genotype-linked variation.

# Inputs to Specify

- Gene and cell counts
- Cell-type or group configuration
- Expression and technical-noise parameters

# Expected Outputs

- Gene-by-cell count matrix
- Cell metadata
- Simulation parameters

# Limitations and Guardrails

- Reference-free simulators can miss dataset-specific correlation and protocol effects.
- Use independent QC to evaluate sparsity, depth, and cell-type separation.

# Questions This Record Can Ground

- What technical artifacts should a scRNA-seq simulation include?
- How is a genotype-aware scRNA-seq workflow different from a generic Splatter run?
